claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the compared equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after identical thermomechanical processing.
Variations in local chemical short-range order modulate stacking-fault energy in these FCC alloys.
Variations in local chemical short-range order modulate dislocation mobility in these FCC alloys.
SRO-mediated changes in stacking-fault energy and dislocation mobility cause differences in yield strength, strain hardening, and failure.
The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy has a more uniform SRO and a more balanced SFE than its lower-component subsets.
Reducing constituent count produces more pronounced local chemical clustering.
Reducing constituent count changes local lattice distortion.
Reducing the number of constituent elements changes the probability distribution of local atomic environments.
The relatively uniform SRO and SFE proposed for the quinary alloy favor stable dislocation slip and balanced strain hardening.
Local clustering and lattice distortions in the lower-component alloys lower or otherwise alter local SFE.
Altered local SFE modifies dislocation nucleation and mobility.
Altered local SFE can change the balance between dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will show measurable differences in yield strength and strain-hardening rate.
Possible lower-component responses include reduced yield strength, earlier twinning, or less uniform slip.
The proposed explanation is restricted to single-phase FCC alloys given identical thermomechanical treatments and tested in room-temperature uniaxial tension at controlled strain rates.
Differences in processing or test parameters may introduce effects not accounted for by the proposed SRO-SFE mechanism.
The direction and magnitude of mechanical-property changes may depend on which elements are removed.
Grain-boundary characteristics or residual stresses may contribute to the measured differences.
A lack of correlation between mechanical-property differences and SRO/SFE differences would falsify the proposed causal explanation.
